findings.claim: Understanding both frameworks is essential For the exam .
findings.truth: Broken capitalisation and a space before the full stop; reads and narrates badly.

findings.claim: Surah 16:90 states: “Indeed Allah commands you towards justice.”
findings.truth: No published translation reads this way. quran.com (Khattab, The Clear Quran) gives “Indeed, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as generosity to close relatives.” Saheeh International gives “Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct…”

findings.claim: 6-mark model answer names 'Source: Surah 16:90 — Indeed Allah commands you towards justice'
findings.truth: Same non-standard wording as F2. Students are told to quote sources in the 6-mark question, so the wording they copy must be a real translation.

findings.claim: 12-mark ladder pastes the board's level descriptors and says “Max Level 2 if no reference to religion.”
findings.truth: 'Level 2' is a banned band name and the descriptors are the board's own wording. The underlying fact (an answer with no religious reference cannot go above 4–6) is kept in house vocabulary.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list; spec 4.4.1 (12-mark question is the AO2 question)

findings.claim: Match question labels angels and predestination “Sunni Six Articles only”.
findings.truth: Shi'a Muslims also believe in angels and in Allah's decree; those beliefs are simply not listed among the five roots. 'only' teaches a false denial.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.1; the lesson's own text says Sunni belief 'separately lists' them

findings.claim: Surah 16:90 states: “Indeed Allah commands you towards justice.”
findings.truth: Same misquotation as F2, repeated in the Adalat paragraph.

findings.claim: Surah 112 … “He is Allah, the One. Allah is Eternal and Absolute. None is born of Him, He is unborn. There is none like unto Him.”
findings.truth: Not any published translation. Yusuf Ali: “Say: He is Allah, the One and Only; Allah, the Eternal, Absolute; He begetteth not, nor is He begotten; And there is none like unto Him.” Surah 112 is the one scripture named in the spec for this unit, so questions may be set on it and students memorise the wording.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.5.1 'Tawhid (the Oneness of God), Qur'an Surah 112'; Wikipedia, Al-Ikhlas (Yusuf Ali, Saheeh International, Pickthall)

findings.claim: 12-mark ladder with 'Max Level 2' and pasted board descriptors.
…demonstrates “reasoned consideration of different points of view” — essential for reaching Level 4.
findings.truth: 'Level 4' is a banned band name and the quoted phrase is the board's own level wording.

findings.claim: 12-mark ladder with 'Max Level 2' and pasted board descriptors.
To reach Level 4 (10–12 marks), you must argue both sides…
findings.truth: 'Level 4' is a banned band name; the mark range is right, so only the label changes.

findings.claim: Surah 23:102–103 … “Those whose scales are heavy [with good deeds] will be the successful ones. But those whose scales are light will have lost their souls; in hell they will abide.”
findings.truth: A rewording. quran.com (Khattab): “As for those whose scale is heavy [with good deeds], it is they who will be successful. But those whose scale is light, they will have doomed themselves, staying in Hell forever.”

findings.claim: 12-mark ladder with 'Max Level 2' and pasted board descriptors.
“A well-applied source can earn up to 2 of the 6 marks”, and every 6-mark model answer is split 'First belief (1–2) + Second belief (1–2) + Source named and applied (1–2)'.
findings.truth: The spec fixes the question at 6 marks (AO1) but publishes no split inside it. The 2-mark weighting for the source is asserted, not sourced, and appears in all four lessons. Options: (a) keep it — it is a reasonable house heuristic; (b) soften to 'you must name and apply a source or you cannot reach full marks', which is safe and needs no board mark scheme; (c) verify against a real mark scheme before keeping a number. Recommend (b).
findings.evidence: spec lines 269 and 1826–1834 (structure 1, 1, 4, 6, 12; AO1 in the first four questions) — no internal split given
findings.ruling: Leave (fleet-wide RS relabel / spec publishes no split).

findings.claim: Adam was placed in the Garden of Eden with Hawwa (Eve).
findings.truth: 'Garden of Eden' is the biblical name; the Qur'an says al-Jannah, 'the Garden'. Common in textbooks and not mark-affecting, so no edit.

findings.claim: Prophets … are considered sinless (ma'sum) and perfectly obedient to God.
findings.truth: Stated flatly for all Muslims. 'Isma / ma'sum is pressed hardest in Shi'a theology, which extends it to the Imams; Sunni theology holds prophets protected from major sin. The lesson's own Imamate section handles the Shi'a side correctly, so no edit.

summary: Doctrine, terminology, named figures and dates are sound and the Sunni/Shi'a split is attributed correctly throughout; every answer key recomputes as correct. The real faults are scripture wording — Surah 112 (the one prescribed text), 16:90 and 23:102-103 were paraphrased inside quotation marks — and the 12-mark ladders, which paste the board's level descriptors and carry the banned band name 'Level 2' in all four lessons plus 'Level 4' in two exam tips.
